title: Product Safety
intro: A product-safety hazard catalogue over the goods corpus: seven hazard classes, the mechanism that produces the injury, the exposure route, the product domains it reaches, the three-tier control hierarchy, the indicative regulatory anchors, and the field signals that precede a recall. Read beside the product taxonomy — the same object, taken as a source of harm rather than as a good.

classes.label: Chemical exposure
classes.desc: The product carries a substance that enters the body by ingestion, inhalation or skin contact — deliberately, as an ingredient, or as a residue, contaminant or migrant.

classes.label: Food contact
classes.desc: The product touches food and transfers something into it: packaging migrants, coatings, or an article not intended for food use.

classes.label: Mechanical
classes.desc: The product's geometry, mass or moving parts produce injury by impact, cutting, crushing, choking or falling.

classes.label: Thermal and fire
classes.desc: The product reaches a temperature that burns, or ignites, or feeds a fire once ignited.

classes.label: Electrical and energy
classes.desc: Stored or mains energy escapes the enclosure: shock through failed insulation, or the violent failure of a cell.

classes.label: Child-specific
classes.desc: Hazards that are tolerable for an adult and severe for a child — the class where size and behaviour, not the product's function, decide the injury.

classes.label: Digital and software
classes.desc: The product's behaviour is set by software, so a defect, a lost function or a remote actor can produce a physical hazard.

hazards.label: Pesticide residue in food
hazards.mechanism: An active substance or its metabolites remain on or in produce after harvest and reach the consumer through the diet, above or below the residue level set for that crop.
hazards.outcome: Chronic dietary exposure; acute effects at high residues; the assessment question is the residue level against the acceptable daily intake and the acute reference dose.

controls.inherent: Grow without the substance, or choose substances with a residue profile that clears before harvest.
controls.safeguarding: Maximum residue levels enforced at the border and at retail; washing and peeling reduce surface residues but not systemic ones.
controls.information: Residue monitoring published per substance and crop, so a consumer can see which combinations are repeatedly found.

signals: repeat findings on one crop
emergency authorisation for a substance withdrawn elsewhere
import batch rejections

hazards.label: Additive exposure above accepted intake
hazards.mechanism: A colour, preservative, sweetener or emulsifier is present at a level that, taken across the products a person actually eats, exceeds the acceptable daily intake — or is present without being declared.
hazards.outcome: Dose-dependent effects in sensitive groups; undeclared additives defeat avoidance for allergy and intolerance.

controls.inherent: Reformulate so the additive is not needed — stabilise, preserve or colour by process rather than by addition.
controls.safeguarding: Restricted lists with maximum levels per food category; intake assessment against the acceptable daily intake.
controls.information: Ingredient declaration by class and name, so a consumer can total their own exposure across products.

signals: same additive across a whole category
reformulation announcements
intake studies exceeding the accepted daily intake in children

hazards.label: Contaminants formed in processing
hazards.mechanism: Heat, smoke or fermentation generates a substance that was not in the raw material — acrylamide from asparagine and sugars in fried or baked starch, polycyclic aromatics from smoke, ethyl carbamate in spirits.
hazards.outcome: Genotoxic and carcinogenic exposure that cannot be removed by washing, because it is in the product's substance.

controls.inherent: Change the process — lower the temperature, shorten the time, blanch before frying, control the precursor.
controls.safeguarding: Benchmark levels and mitigation plans for the categories where the contaminant forms.
controls.information: Guidance for catering and home cooking on the browning point that raises the level.

signals: category-wide benchmark exceedance
mitigation plans failing on repeat sampling

hazards.label: Fragrance and preservative sensitisers
hazards.mechanism: A fragrance allergen or a preservative reaches the skin at a concentration that sensitises it, so that later contact produces dermatitis at a dose that was previously tolerated.
hazards.outcome: Allergic contact dermatitis; once sensitised, the person reacts to many products, not only the one that sensitised them.

controls.inherent: Remove the sensitiser from the formula, or reduce it below the labelling threshold.
controls.safeguarding: Restricted concentrations for the recognised sensitisers; leave-on products treated more strictly than rinse-off.
controls.information: Ingredient list with the allergens named, so a sensitised person can read the label rather than the marketing.

signals: patch-test clusters for one allergen
rise in a category's reported reactions
reformulation without a label change

hazards.label: Lead and cadmium migration from consumer articles
hazards.mechanism: A metal in the article's material — glaze, pigment, solder, alloy, recycled plastic — migrates into food, drink or the hand and then the mouth.
hazards.outcome: Neurodevelopmental harm in children at exposures far below the acute threshold; the harm is cumulative and irreversible.

controls.inherent: Do not use the metal in the material: lead-free glaze, cadmium-free pigment, virgin polymer where recycled stock cannot be characterised.
controls.safeguarding: Migration limits tested per article type, with the test condition matched to how the article is used.
controls.information: Declaration of conformity and the test report behind it, available to the distributor rather than only to the importer.

signals: border rejections of one origin
cheap jewellery clusters
recycled stock with an unverified provenance

hazards.label: Volatile organic compounds from furnishings and finishes
hazards.mechanism: Formaldehyde from board adhesives, solvents from paints and lacquers, and finishes on textiles evaporate into indoor air over months.
hazards.outcome: Irritation and respiratory symptoms in the short term; formaldehyde is a recognised carcinogen, so the concern is chronic indoor concentration.

controls.inherent: Use board and adhesive classes that do not emit, and water-based finishes.
controls.safeguarding: Emission classes and mandatory declaration for the product as placed on the market.
controls.information: Ventilation guidance and the emission class stated on the product rather than in a technical annex.

standards: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/988 — general product safety (emission information)
signals: indoor-air complaints clustered in new buildings
one board supplier behind many brands

hazards.label: Packaging migrants into food
hazards.mechanism: A monomer, plasticiser, ink component or mineral oil moves from the packaging into the food, more readily at higher temperature, longer contact and higher fat content.
hazards.outcome: Chronic low-dose exposure to substances never assessed as food; the level depends on storage conditions, not on the food's recipe.

controls.inherent: Choose a packaging material whose migrants are authorised and whose barrier keeps the food-side layer from the ink and the adhesive.
controls.safeguarding: Migration testing under the worst foreseeable condition of use, and functional barriers where the material requires one.
controls.information: Food-contact declaration and the conditions of use, including whether the article is single-use.

signals: migration above the limit in one simulant
recycled-content streams without a decontamination step

hazards.label: Non-food article reused for food
hazards.mechanism: A container, bucket, crate or decorative vessel made for another purpose is used for food, so a material never assessed for food contact becomes the food's surface.
hazards.outcome: Unauthorised migrants, including ink and industrial-grade polymer additives, at levels no food-contact test would have allowed.

controls.inherent: Mark the article unambiguously as not for food, so the reuse is hard to make by accident.
controls.safeguarding: Market surveillance at the catering supplier rather than at the consumer.
controls.information: The food-contact symbol, and its absence read as a warning rather than as a formality.

signals: catering supplies sold without a declaration
decorative ceramics sold beside tableware

hazards.label: Small parts and choking
hazards.mechanism: A component small enough to enter a child's mouth lodges in the airway, or a larger part breaks into such a component under the force a child applies.
hazards.outcome: Airway obstruction; the injury is decided by the part's size and shape against the child's anatomy, not by the product's purpose.

controls.inherent: Design the part out, or make it too large to swallow and too strong to break into a swallowable fragment.
controls.safeguarding: Small-parts cylinder and tension tests on the components a child can reach.
controls.information: Age marking and the warning that the product is not for children under the stated age.

standards: EN 71-1 — toy mechanical and physical properties
signals: detachment complaints on one mould
one component supplier across many toy lines

hazards.label: Sharp edges and points
hazards.mechanism: A cut edge, a burr, a point or a glass fragment left by manufacture or exposed by breakage contacts the skin or the eye.
hazards.outcome: Laceration or eye injury; the severity depends on where the edge is reachable, which is an accessibility question before it is a sharpness question.

controls.inherent: Roll, radius or cover the edge at design, rather than adding a guard at the end of the line.
controls.safeguarding: Edge and point tests on the surfaces reachable in normal use, including after the drop the product must survive.
controls.information: Handling and disposal instruction where the edge is inherent to the function, as with a blade.

standards: ISO 12100 — risk assessment and risk reduction
signals: hand-injury reports clustered on one part
tooling wear after a production change

hazards.label: Furniture tip-over
hazards.mechanism: A tall or front-heavy article overturns when a child climbs it or a drawer is loaded, because it is not anchored and its stability margin is small.
hazards.outcome: Crushing injury to a child; the failure is usually the absence of an anchor, not the article's mass.

controls.inherent: Lower the centre of mass, limit drawer travel, and design the anchor point into the article rather than selling it as an accessory.
controls.safeguarding: Stability test with drawers open and with a simulated climber, plus an anchor supplied in the box.
controls.information: Assembly instruction that makes anchoring the default, not an optional extra.

standards: ISO 12100 — risk assessment and risk reduction
signals: anchor kits bought separately
injury reports in rented housing where anchoring is not permitted

hazards.label: Cords and strangulation
hazards.mechanism: A cord, ribbon or loop at neck height catches on play equipment or a cot, and the child's weight closes the loop.
hazards.outcome: Asphyxiation within minutes; the hazard is a dimension and a location, not a material.

controls.inherent: Remove the cord or make it short enough to break away under load.
controls.safeguarding: Cord length and loop limits at the neck and waist, tested in the size range the garment is sold for.
controls.information: Warning on the garment and at the point of sale that the item is not nightwear.

standards: EN 14682 — cords and drawstrings on children's clothing
signals: one style across sizes
blinds sold with a looped pull

hazards.label: Button-cell ingestion
hazards.mechanism: A coin cell released from a toy, remote or greeting card lodges in the oesophagus, where the residual current generates hydroxide and burns the tissue.
hazards.outcome: Perforation and stricture within hours; the injury continues after the cell is removed.

controls.inherent: Solder the cell in, or require a tool for the compartment, so the cell is not a removable part a child can reach.
controls.safeguarding: Compartment security test with the force a child can apply, and a bitter coating on the cell.
controls.information: Warning that names the injury and the action — the child must be taken to emergency care, not made to vomit.

standards: EN 71-1 — toy mechanical and physical properties
signals: compartment opening after a drop
cheap remote controls sold without a screw

hazards.label: High-flux magnet ingestion
hazards.mechanism: Two or more small magnets are swallowed at different times and attract each other across bowel loops.
hazards.outcome: Necrosis, fistula and obstruction; a single magnet is usually benign, which is why the hazard is easy to miss.

controls.inherent: Keep the magnet inside the housing so it is not a part at all, or size it beyond swallowing.
controls.safeguarding: Flux index and size limits for the magnets a child can reach.
controls.information: The warning that a swallowed magnet is a medical emergency even without symptoms.

standards: EN 71-1 — toy mechanical and physical properties
signals: magnet sets sold as adult desk toys
housings that open after impact

hazards.label: Accessible hot surfaces
hazards.mechanism: A surface that must be hot to work is reachable in normal use — a hob, an oven door, a heater grille, a kettle body — and contact occurs faster than the withdrawal reflex.
hazards.outcome: Contact burns, deep in children and the elderly because the skin is thinner and the reflex slower.

controls.inherent: Insulate or double-wall the reachable surface, or reduce the temperature the surface must reach.
controls.safeguarding: Guards and distance, plus a test of the surfaces reachable while the appliance operates.
controls.information: The residual-heat warning and the cooling time stated where the user will see it.

standards: IEC 60335-1 — household and similar electrical appliances
signals: burns reported after the appliance is switched off
one model's door glass

hazards.label: Flammable upholstery and sleepwear
hazards.mechanism: A textile ignites from a small source and burns fast enough that the victim cannot escape, or melts onto the skin.
hazards.outcome: Full-thickness burns over a large area; survival depends on the fabric and the fit, not on the ignition source.

controls.inherent: Choose a fabric and filling that resist ignition, or a design that cannot trap a flame against the body.
controls.safeguarding: Ignition and flame-spread tests matched to the article's use; nightwear held to a stricter standard than daywear.
controls.information: The warning label and the instruction to keep the article away from ignition sources.

signals: loose-fitting nightwear sold as daywear
filling changed without a retest

hazards.label: Insulation failure and electric shock
hazards.mechanism: Creepage, clearance or insulation breaks down under heat, moisture or contamination, so a live conductor becomes reachable.
hazards.outcome: Ventricular fibrillation at mains current in a fraction of a second; the failure can also start a fire.

controls.inherent: Double or reinforced insulation and protective earthing where the class requires it, designed into the layout.
controls.safeguarding: Dielectric strength, creepage and clearance tests after the environmental sequence the product must survive.
controls.information: Rating plate and the conditions of use, including that a charger is not a wet-environment product.

signals: failures concentrated after a humid season
a component change that shortened a creepage path

hazards.label: Lithium-cell thermal runaway
hazards.mechanism: An internal short, overcharge or external abuse drives a cell into exothermic decomposition, which propagates to its neighbours.
hazards.outcome: Jet-flame ejection, ejection of the cell from the enclosure, and a fire that water does not readily extinguish.

controls.inherent: Cell chemistry and format chosen for the abuse the product will see, with a management circuit that cannot be bypassed.
controls.safeguarding: Cell-level tests for overcharge, external short, crush and thermal propagation; enclosure that contains the ejection.
controls.information: Charging instruction, and the warning not to charge unattended or in an exit path.

signals: cell supplier changes
cheap replacement batteries sold for a known model
charging in corridors and stairwells

hazards.label: Loss of a safety function in a connected product
hazards.mechanism: A safety function is implemented in software or depends on a remote service, so an update, a configuration error or a server shutdown removes the protection while the product still appears to work.
hazards.outcome: The hazard the safety function was guarding reappears silently; the user has no signal that protection is gone.

controls.inherent: Keep the safety function local and fail-safe, so that a lost connection leaves the product in a safe state.
controls.safeguarding: Independent verification of the safety function, and update mechanisms that cannot remove it silently.
controls.information: Statement of the product's support lifetime and of what happens to the safety function at end of support.

standards: EU Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30
signals: service shutdown announcements
updates shipped without a safety regression test
support lifetime shorter than the product's use life

hazards.label: Remote manipulation of an actuator
hazards.mechanism: An unauthenticated interface lets a remote party command a lock, a motor, a heater or a camera, turning a software compromise into a physical action.
hazards.outcome: Physical harm or loss of protection at a distance, without the user's device ever being touched.

controls.inherent: No actuator reachable without authentication, and a physical override that does not depend on the network.
controls.safeguarding: Security testing of the shipped firmware and of the update channel, including the default credential.
controls.information: The disclosure route for a found vulnerability, and the response time the vendor commits to.

standards: EU Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30
ISO 12100 — risk assessment and risk reduction
signals: default password across a product line
one cloud provider behind many brands
no coordinated disclosure contact
